profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the backend platform workstream and the analytics/research workstream for an internal engineering initiative studying how teamwork quality signals can be integrated into a software team performance dashboard. The team is preparing a cross-functional pilot for three product squads, where backend will expose derived collaboration events and analytics will compute weekly TWQ-related indicators inspired by the paper summary. The agenda is to align on the event interface, the definition of the weekly handoff, ownership of the shared metric specification, and what 'pilot-ready' means for next Friday's internal demo. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on what backend will deliver, what analytics will consume, and what each side believes will be ready for the pilot review.

members.name: Nina Patel
members.expertise: Event pipelines, service contracts, internal APIs, data reliability
members.background: Nina leads the team that owns the engineering activity event stream used by internal tooling; she previously built audit-log and collaboration telemetry services for large SaaS products.
members.private_state: She wants to avoid reopening the ingestion design and keep her team focused on delivering a minimally disruptive export from the existing event bus before the quarter-end reliability freeze.
hidden_assumptions: A 'weekly dataset' means one finalized Monday morning snapshot covering the previous Monday-Sunday period after late-arriving events have been backfilled.
The 'schema doc' is the current Confluence contract for the v2 collaboration_events feed, because that is the only backend-owned document she considers normative.
Making the pilot 'ready' means the API endpoint is stable, authenticated, and populated for the three squads in staging, even if some derived teamwork dimensions are still computed downstream.
When analytics says they will 'consume team events,' they mean the already-normalized collaboration_events stream rather than raw source-specific records from GitHub, Jira, and Slack.
Any metric logic beyond field-level semantics belongs to analytics once the interface payload is published.

members.name: Leo Martinez
members.expertise: Behavioral metrics, experimentation, product analytics, organizational data modeling
members.background: Leo manages the team building internal dashboards for engineering effectiveness and has a background in socio-technical analysis of software teams, including survey-linked collaboration metrics.
members.private_state: He wants enough granularity to prototype TWQ indicators quickly for the pilot and is trying to avoid another week of data wrangling because stakeholders already expect a visible dashboard slice at Friday's demo.
hidden_assumptions: A 'weekly dataset' means rolling seven-day extracts generated each day so the dashboard can always show the latest week-to-date view.
The 'schema doc' refers to the shared Google Doc where analytics and PM annotated which fields map to communication, coordination, and trust proxies.
Making the pilot 'ready' means the dashboard shows interpretable TWQ indicators for all three squads with at least basic validation against known team activity patterns.
When backend offers 'team events,' it includes enough raw provenance or source-level detail to recompute aggregation logic if the TWQ formulas change.
The event definitions were effectively settled in last Tuesday's product review where PM, analytics, and design discussed the pilot story, even though backend was not in that meeting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree that analytics will receive the 'weekly dataset' before the demo.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this is a single finalized weekly snapshot delivered once per week after backfills, covering the previous full week.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this is a rolling seven-day dataset refreshed daily so the dashboard remains current through the demo week.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In software coordination, 'weekly dataset' sounds standard and sufficient on the surface; both assume the cadence is obvious from their own team's routines, so neither thinks to unpack whether 'weekly' describes the reporting window or the delivery frequency.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to 'the schema doc' as the thing everyone is already aligned to.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the backend-owned Confluence page for the v2 collaboration_events contract.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the shared Google Doc with annotated field mappings used by analytics and PM during pilot planning.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both documents are genuinely used in the project and each has been casually called 'the schema doc'; because both are talking about field alignment rather than disputing content line by line, the reference mismatch passes unnoticed.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the goal is to have the pilot 'ready for Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks 'ready' means the interface is stable in staging, sample data is flowing, and consumers can start integrating.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks 'ready' means the dashboard already displays usable TWQ indicators for the three squads with sanity-checked outputs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both criteria are reasonable within their functions and are often compressed into the same milestone language; because the meeting is framed as coordination rather than milestone negotiation, they do not probe the acceptance threshold behind 'ready.'

misalignment_points.topic: Scope of the team events handoff
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree backend will provide the 'team events' needed for TWQ metrics.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this includes normalized collaboration_events records with canonical fields such as actor, team_id, event_type, and timestamp.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this includes source-level detail or provenance fields from GitHub, Jira, and Slack so analytics can revise aggregation logic and derive alternate teamwork indicators later.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both sides believe normalized events are obviously part of 'team events,' but they silently differ on whether provenance and raw detail are included; because the immediate conversation centers on getting data flowing, the boundary of the handoff remains implicit.
